## What managing River North takes.

### Brick-and-timber lofts
The converted warehouses around Kinzie, Hubbard, and the gallery district have exposed timber, original masonry, and freight-elevator retrofits. We treat the maintenance profile of loft conversions as its own discipline.

### Short-term-rental enforcement
River North's location makes it a magnet for unauthorized short-term rentals. We help boards adopt leasing amendments, pursue violations, and use Chicago's shared-housing rules, including the prohibited-buildings list, to keep buildings residential.

### High-rise turnover and transitions
As developer-controlled boards turn over in newer towers, we coordinate transition studies, warranty claims, and first-year budgets that put new associations on solid ground.

## River North boards ask us first.

### Can CenterPoint help our River North board control Airbnb and short-term rentals?
Yes. We work with association counsel to draft and enforce leasing amendments, monitor listings, process violations, and register buildings on the City of Chicago's shared-housing prohibited-buildings list where the board chooses to opt out.

### Do you manage loft condominium buildings in River North?
Yes. Brick-and-timber loft conversions are a management specialty of ours, from freight elevator modernization and sprinkler systems to the masonry and window programs that keep century-old warehouse buildings sound.

### Does CenterPoint manage associations in River North?
Yes. CenterPoint Association Management provides condominium, HOA, and townhome association management in River North, Chicago (ZIP 60611, 60654). Every association gets a dedicated manager, monthly financial reporting, and board support grounded in Illinois association law.

### How much does association management cost in River North?
Management starts at $20 per unit per month, quoted as a flat monthly fee based on your association's size, building systems, financial complexity, and service scope. It is never a percentage of your budget. See [pricing](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/pricing) for what drives the fee.

### How does a River North association switch to CenterPoint?
Plan on a managed 30 to 60 day transition after your board gives notice under its current contract. We retrieve records from the outgoing manager, set up banking and vendor relationships, notify owners, and open board and resident access. ### How should a River North board compare management companies?
Compare at least three firms on the same terms: an active Illinois community association management firm license, a licensed manager, a flat monthly fee in writing, after-hours emergency coverage, and a written transition plan.
